question.text: Ms. Priya Shah, a Company Secretary with 5 years of NPO audit experience, applies for SIA empanelment. Under SEBI (Intermediaries) Regulations 2008, the 'fit and proper person' criterion (Schedule II) requires assessment of:

answer.text: Only the applicant's professional qualification, nothing more
Integrity, reputation, absence of convictions, financial soundness, and absence of regulatory bars
Only the employer NPO's track record — not the applicant individual

explanation.text: The Logic: The 'fit and proper person' test under the SEBI (Intermediaries) Regulations is a multi-factor assessment. Schedule II of those regulations requires the regulator to consider integrity, honesty, reputation and character; absence of criminal convictions (including economic offences); financial soundness; and absence of regulatory bars or sanctions. Professional qualification alone is only one input. The Trap: Option A treats qualification as the only criterion. Option B reduces the test to net-worth/CIBIL alone, omitting integrity and reputation. Option D shifts the test from the applicant to the employer — the fit-and-proper assessment is personal to the applicant. Note: The cited SIA workbook pages reference SIA registration and codes of conduct but do not specifically state the SEBI Intermediaries Regulations Schedule II fit-and-proper criteria (integrity, reputation, convictions, financial soundness, regulatory bars). The framing above reflects the general SEBI intermediary regulatory framework rather than a workbook-page citation.
